Original learning chapter · updated 9 September 2026. Equations and examples explain concepts; they are not test acceptance or a support matrix.

Prerequisites: 02 · Matrices and homogeneous transforms, 12 · Numerical accuracy, tests and honest evidence

A sequence of meshes is not yet a simulation system

An animation describes change over time. It can be authored by keyframes, computed from a formula, produced by a learned model or generated by a physical solver. Playing saved meshes in a viewer proves that the frames can be displayed. It does not establish a general animation API, a physical law or differentiability through the process that created the frames.

Interpolating vertex positions assumes corresponding vertices and compatible topology. Simply interpolating rotation-matrix entries can destroy orthogonality and introduce scale or shear. Quaternion interpolation and skinning require their own conventions; they are not supplied by a generic frame player. Sampling time also matters: output at 60 frames per second does not mean the solver should take steps of exactly one sixtieth of a second.

Worked example

A ball starts at height two metres with zero vertical velocity. Ignoring air and contact, gravity g=9.81 metres per second squared gives height 1.95095 metres after 0.1 seconds. This is an analytic pre-contact fixture, so a numerical integrator can be checked before complicated collision behavior is introduced.

Contact adds forces and numerical difficulty

A simple penalty model treats penetration as spring compression and adds damping while contact is active. The spring stores energy, gravity exchanges potential and kinetic energy, and damping removes energy. A stiff spring requires careful timestep selection; otherwise the numerical method can inject energy or miss the collision. Halving the integration step and comparing trajectories tests numerical sensitivity.

Conservation means accounting for all transfers. A damped collision is expected to lose mechanical energy to unmodeled heat, so demanding constant mechanical energy would reject the intended model. A stylized volume-preserving squash can make an impact readable while still not solving internal stresses or elastic waves in the mesh.

Try it yourself

Does doubling playback FPS improve the physics?

Answer

Not by itself. It changes presentation sampling. Improving the solver may require a smaller integration timestep, better contact handling or a better physical model.

gffx boundary

The saved deformation clips and elastic-ball scene are finite demonstrations. The ball uses a centroid/contact calculation plus display squash, not a differentiable mesh soft-body solver. The planned animation operations and general simulation work remain separate roadmap items. No physical wood-material calibration, hard-real-time guarantee or energy-conserving general solver is claimed.
